key_insight: Aes3D presents a dedicated framework to evaluate and predict the aesthetic quality of 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes by learning from multi-view renders and 3D-aware cues, bridging the gap between low‑level fidelity metrics and high‑level visual appeal.
problem_solved: Existing 3D evaluation metrics focus on reconstruction fidelity and realism but ignore higher‑level aesthetic attributes (composition, harmony, visual appeal); there is no standardized benchmark or model for assessing aesthetics of 3DGS content.
method: Create a human‑rated benchmark of 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes and render multi‑view images per scene for perceptual labeling.
Extract image aesthetic features from each view (pretrained aesthetic/vision backbones) and aggregate across views using attention/pooling to form a scene‑level representation.
Augment aggregated visual features with 3DGS‑specific cues (e.g., splat distribution, color statistics, camera composition) and train a regression/ranking model to predict aesthetic scores.
impact: Provides practitioners a tool and benchmark to quantify and optimize visual appeal in 3DGS pipelines, enabling automated quality guidance, aesthetic-driven content generation, and standardized evaluation beyond fidelity metrics.
visual_elements: Multi‑view render grid of a 3DGS scene with per‑view aesthetic scores and aggregated scene score
Pipeline diagram: 3DGS scene → multi‑view rendering → feature extraction → view aggregation → aesthetic scorer
Bar/boxplot comparing Aes3D aesthetic scores against traditional fidelity metrics (PSNR/LPIPS) to show orthogonality
Radar or attribute icons showing component contributions (composition, color harmony, lighting, detail)
paper_title: Aes3D: Aesthetic Assessment in 3D Gaussian Splatting
paper_authors: Chuanzhi Xu, Boyu Wei, Haoxian Zhou, Xuanhua Yin, Zihan Deng
